title: Mittag--Leffler vanishing
statement:
Let $(A_n,f_n:A_{n+1}\to A_n)_{n\ge1}$ be an inverse system [def-weil-inverse-system] of finite abelian groups. It satisfies the Mittag--Leffler condition [def-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler-system] and $R^1\varprojlim_n A_n=0$, with the derived functor understood as in [lem-pc-derived-limit-roos-abelian-groups].

Consequently, if $(K_n)$ is a countable tower in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with derived limit as in [def-weil-derived-limit] and $i\in\mathbf Z$, and every $H^{i-1}(K_n)$ is finite, the canonical Milnor map
$$H^i(R\varprojlim_n K_n)\longrightarrow\varprojlim_n H^i(K_n)$$
of [lem-pc-derived-limit-milnor-sequence] is an isomorphism. In particular this holds in all degrees for a tower of finite abelian groups placed in degree zero.

For the construction [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit], the precise corresponding assertion is the following: let $T$ be a scheme and $(A,I)$ an adic coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Let $M_\bullet\in D(\operatorname{Tow}_A(T))$, write $M_n=\operatorname{ev}_nM_\bullet$, fix $i\in\mathbf Z$, and let $U$ be a weakly contractible quasi-compact object of $T_{\mathrm{Proet}}$, as in [prop-weil-pbc-roos-triangle]. If every abelian group $H^{i-1}(U,M_n)$ is finite, then its canonical map
$$H^i(U,R\varprojlim M_\bullet)\longrightarrow\varprojlim_n H^i(U,M_n)$$
is an isomorphism.

external.place: (*Source note:* the vanishing is Stacks Project, More on Algebra, Lemma 15.88.1 (3) (Tag [07KW](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07KW): if $(A_n)$ is Mittag--Leffler then $R^1\lim A_n=0$, i.e. the system is right acyclic for $\lim$), and the identification of the Milnor map is Lemma 15.88.10 (Tag [07KY](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07KY)).

proof.text: Fix $n$. The subgroups $\operatorname{Im}(A_m\to A_n)$ decrease as $m\ge n$ increases. Their finite cardinalities have a minimum, attained at some $c\ge n$; every subsequent subgroup is contained in the one at $c$ and has the same cardinality, hence equals it. This is exactly the ML condition of [def-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler-system].

source.place: Homology, Tag 02N0 (definition-Mittag-Leffler), specialized to finite groups

proof.text: For arbitrary $y=(y_n)\in\prod_n A_n$, let $E_N$ be the set of tuples $(x_1,\ldots,x_N)$ with $x_j-f_j(x_{j+1})=y_j$ for $1\le j<N$. It is finite and nonempty: choose $x_N=0$ and successively define $x_j=y_j+f_j(x_{j+1})$ downwards. Forgetting the last coordinate defines $E_{N+1}\to E_N$. For fixed $N$, the images of $E_m$ in the finite set $E_N$ form a decreasing chain of nonempty subsets, Choose an image of minimum cardinality, attained at an index $c\ge N$. Every image at $m\ge c$ is contained in it and has at least that minimum cardinality, hence equals it. Thus this set tower is ML.

proof.text: Apply Mathlib nonempty_sections_of_finite_cofiltered_system directly to the finite nonempty prefix-solution tower of Step 2. Its compatible section gives x_n by taking the last coordinate of its length n+1 prefix. Compatibility identifies that coordinate with the preceding coordinate in the next prefix, whose defining equation is x_n-f_n(x_(n+1))=y_n. Thus the Roos map is surjective. This finite special case needs no general Mittag--Leffler nonempty-limit lemma.

proof.text: By [lem-pc-derived-limit-roos-abelian-groups], $R^1\varprojlim A_n$ is naturally the cokernel of this very map $1-s$. Its surjectivity from Step 3 makes that cokernel zero, proving the vanishing.

For $(K_n)$ and $i$ in the statement, the transition maps induce a tower of finite abelian groups $H^{i-1}(K_n)$. Apply Steps 1--4 to it. In the natural short exact sequence of [lem-pc-derived-limit-milnor-sequence], the left term is therefore zero. Exactness makes the canonical map injective and surjective, hence an isomorphism. For finite groups in degree zero, the preceding cohomology groups are finite (either the given groups or zero) for every $i$, giving the stated special case.

For $M_\bullet,U,i$ in the last paragraph, use exactly the short exact sequence of [prop-weil-pbc-roos-triangle]. Its left term is $R^1\varprojlim_n H^{i-1}(U,M_n)$, which is zero by Steps 1--4, because these are finite abelian groups by the stated hypothesis. The middle-to-right arrow is precisely the asserted canonical Milnor map; its kernel is zero and it is surjective by that sequence, so it is an isomorphism. No identification of finite abelian groups with arbitrary coefficient-module sheaves is used. For an arbitrary specified Roos triangle, complete the identity maps on its two product objects to a morphism into the canonical triangle from prop-weil-pbc-roos-triangle. Two invertible components make the third component g invertible. The first square says p=g followed by the canonical projection. Applying cohomology and evaluation, then the limit-projection equations, identifies the specified b with H^i(U,g) followed by the canonical Milnor map, so it too is invertible.

blueprint_update.statement:
A tower of finite abelian groups satisfies the Mittag--Leffler condition and
has $\varprojlim{}^1=0$. Consequently, for the derived inverse-limit
construction of [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit], the canonical Milnor
map is an isomorphism for such a tower.

proof.text:
Descending chains of subgroups of a finite group stabilize, so the tower is
Mittag--Leffler and $\varprojlim{}^1=0$ by the product-cokernel description
of $\varprojlim{}^1$; the exact sequence of
[prop-weil-pbc-roos-triangle] then identifies the Milnor map.
